notes:
A licence activation that could not be confirmed is now remembered anyway, so
it cannot be paid for twice.

Activating Docket takes one of your three activations at the moment the payment
provider grants it. Docket then checks that activation before carrying on. If
the connection dropped between those two steps — the activation granted, the
check never answered — Docket forgot which activation it had just been given.
The next run asked for another one.

On a poor connection that could repeat, and each repeat used a real activation:
ones you could not see, on a Mac you were already sitting at, and could not
release because nothing had recorded them.

Docket now writes the activation down the moment it is granted, before checking
it. The record says only which activation this Mac holds. It is not treated as
proof that the licence is valid — that is still checked separately and can
still fail — it only makes sure something you have already paid for is never
bought a second time.

If you think this has happened to you, the activations can be returned: write
to the address on the contact page and it will be sorted out the same day.

Nothing in your audits changes in this release.
